content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Robert Weber (E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

The team notes: 5 notes say he's a full-time Payroll Specialist, so max is write (since Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code). They recommend write.

Note 6 from Security DB says he's a contractor with basic security training, recommending read.

There's a conflict here. Five notes say full-time Payroll Specialist, one (Security DB) says contractor with basic training.

Which to trust? The security database note says contractor with basic security training. Hmm. Let me think about how these teams' notes work. The HR agent, IT agent, Finance agent, Compliance agent, Facilities agent, Security agent each write notes with employee facts.

Note 6 is from Security DB (the Security agent presumably). It says contractor with basic security training. The other five say full-time.

Conflict: employment type differs. The Security note claims "Security DB shows... contractor with basic security training, not full-time."

Hmm, which is more authoritative? Typically for employment type, HR would be authoritative. But here the notes listed don't label which agent each came from explicitly; they just say "Note 1 (ticket 1)" etc. The comment in note 6 says "Security DB shows...". Note 2 says "IT DB confirms". Note 3 "Finance DB confirms". Note 4 "Compliance DB confirms". Note 5 "Facilities DB confirms". Note 1 seems HR/role info.

So we have a discrepancy in employment type: full_time vs contractor. The majority say full-time. The security note says contractor.

The policy differs: full_time Payroll Specialist -> max write. contractor with basic training -> max read.

Given conflicting facts, I need to make a decision. The majority (5 notes) agree on full_time Payroll Specialist. The security note is a single dissenting note. Typically, HR is authoritative for employment type. Note 1 appears to be from HR (role, employment type).

I think the reasonable approach is to follow the majority / HR-confirmed facts: full-time Payroll Specialist, so max access is write (not admin). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant write.

Let me decide: write.

I'll submit with reasoning citing that Robert Weber is full-time Payroll Specialist per HR/IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities, Source Code owned by Engineer, so admin not permitted; cap write; requested admin exceeds max -> grant write.
